consensus_summary: Consensus treats scarlet’s dominant Christian sense as the deep stain of sin/guilt (Isa 1:18), with well-attested secondary senses of sacrificial/atoning blood (Rahab’s cord, scarlet wool in rites, Heb 9:19), royalty/luxury, and the corrupt harlot/Babylon system (Rev 17–18).
book_summary: Scarlet is covenant blood displayed outwardly, together with its counterfeit by those who wear the outward form without the substance.
consensus_core_identification: sin-stain (primary) paired with atoning/covenant blood (common alternative)
book_core_identification: outward display of covenant blood and its counterfeit
boundary_disagreement: Book retains the blood/atonement and Rev-harlot cases but subordinates or re-reads the dominant Isa 1:18 sin-stain and pure-luxury readings as instances of true versus counterfeit covenant-blood display rather than independent primary senses.
rationale: The blood/covenant and Rev-counterfeit strands already appear as common consensus alternatives; the book keeps that referent category while narrowing its center to ‘covenant blood displayed’ and re-classifying the harlot’s scarlet as counterfeit form-without-substance. This is boundary refinement, not replacement of the core or pure novelty.
strongest_objection: Isa 1:18 (explicitly cited) supplies the consensus’s strongest primary sense of sin-stain, which the book’s wording does not foreground and appears to reframe.
